title: Add benchmark-lab end-to-end reporting pipeline v141
author: Maya Patel
description: This PR wires up the next-generation end-to-end reporting pipeline for the benchmark lab (v141). Motivation: consolidate representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and telemetry into a single repeatable pipeline that produces per-model/per-variant reports and feeds dashboards and anomaly detectors. Scope: 1) add a new reporting pipeline orchestration (benchmark-lab/pipelines/reporting/v141/pipeline.yaml) that supports configurable suite graphs and multi-variant aggregation; 2) add representative workload runners for web-chat, summarization, and embeddings (benchmark-lab/runners/representative/*) with improved synthetic load profiles and config templates; 3) add profiling baseline definitions (benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v141.json) and a small set of kernel-selection telemetry hooks; 4) telemetry and schema updates (infra/telemetry/metrics_schema.yaml) to export unit-cost, tail-latency buckets, and KV-cache hit ratios; 5) CI job to run the end-to-end pipeline in the perf cluster (ci/benchmark-lab.yaml); 6) dashboards/reporting_v141.json and docs updates. Checklist: - [x] pipeline orchestration implemented - [x] representative runners added and smoke-tested - [x] profiling baselines captured for 3 models - [x] telemetry schema updated and validated - [x] CI job added and passing on perf cluster - [x] docs and runbook updated. Testing notes: unit tests for runners and pipeline steps added, integration test runs on the perf cluster captured in CI artifacts, and an e2e run was performed against a canary GPU pool. Rollout plan: deploy pipeline in staging, run two full suites across representative hardware (A100, H100, g4dn), validate dashboards and auto-alerts for regression thresholds, then enable in production nightly schedule. Backwards compatibility: schema additions are additive and backwards compatible with v140 consumers. See linked Linear items ENG-3421 (reporting orchestration) and ENG-5620 (profiling baseline capture).
